text:
incident-bot: 🔔 PAGER: gpu-pool gw-prod-high under sustained queue growth (>95% utilization) and driver errors. Severity: high. Alerting teams: eng-sre, eng-runtime, infra.

sasha: saw the pager, joining. what's the immediate customer impact?

oliver: support reports a handful of customers seeing 5-20s generation latency spikes and intermittent 503s on high-throughput routes (embedding and chat). Not widespread but consistent with queueing.

raj: looks like autoscaler attempted scale but nodes didn't register. Cloud API returned rate-limited errors and then 403 for a subset — hitting soft quota for accelerators in region eu-west-1.

maria: also seeing a wave of CUDA Xid 701/3/4 on nodes that did register. Kernel driver shows OOM+GPU reset traces. Effective GPU capacity is much lower than reported.

lee: ok, triage plan: 1) isolate flapping nodes, 2) reduce admission to protect latency SLO, 3) try emergency reserved capacity if quotas are blocking, 4) customer comms. Who will take #1 and #2?

raj: I'll take node isolation. Running a fast grep across node logs to list ones with repeated Xid.

maria: I'll throttle model admission and roll a canary policy to fallback to CPU-backed lower-tier model for non-critical routes. Pushing policy now.

sasha: on customer comms, can we get a short internal impact statement for PM/CS? Oliver, can you draft a quick blurb we can use?

oliver: on it. Draft: "We are investigating increased latency and intermittent failures for some inference requests in eu-west-1 caused by GPU node instability and autoscaler failures. Mitigation actions are in progress; we'll provide updates every 15 minutes." Thoughts?

sasha: good. Add estimated ETA: 1h for containment.

incident-bot: runbook step: mark nodes unhealthy -> drain -> cordon.

raj: listing nodes with Xid errors... running:

```
ssh ops@jump
sudo journalctl -u gpu-driver -o cat | grep -E "Xid 701|Xid 3|OOM" -A2
```

raj: found 6 nodes with repeated Xid resets: gw-node-12, gw-node-14, gw-node-19, gw-node-21, gw-node-27, gw-node-33. Many show kernel OOM around same timeframe.

maria: checking nvidia-smi on one:

```
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY -i 0
Attached GPUs : 1
FB Memory Usage
    Total                     : 4096 MiB
    Used                      : 3986 MiB
    Free                      : 110 MiB

+ gpu reset detected: GPU 0000:65:00.0 Reset Reason: Xid 701
```

lee: raj, please drain those nodes and ensure we don't evict critical workloads that can take longer than 5m to restart. Use graceful drain flag.

raj: starting drain: `kubectl drain gw-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300` repeating for list.

maria: can you also flip autoscaler to manual and increase target nodes to avoid oscillation? The autoscaler is seeing registration failures and is thrashing.

sasha: good call. raj, you have rights to set node-group desired_count?

raj: yes, setting autoscaler to warm target +4 to compensate, but cloud quota still a blocker for 2 nodes. Hitting API 429s then 403 for additional requests.

incident-bot: attached logs indicate creation requests failing with error: "insufficient accelarator quota" (sic) and transient 429s.

lee: open a quota request with cloud console, but also fallback: if we can't get more GPUs immediately, start evacuating jobs to lower-memory quantized models and reduce batch sizes to cut memory pressure. Maria, can you trigger model fallback?

maria: initiating model fallback policy now. Reduced batch_size from 16->4, enabled 4-bit quantized variant for heavy routes. Pushing config:

```
PATCH /runtime/config
{
  "routes": {
    "/v1/chat": { "batch_size": 4, "fallback_model": "redwood-q4f32" }
  }
}
```

maria: also enabling prefix KV caching for chat to lower token generation load for repeat users.

oliver: CS updated customers with the internal blurb and noted limited impact window estimate 1h->2h. They'll escalate any high-severity customers.

sasha: internal priority: protect SLO for paid customers > free tier. Can we apply route-level throttles to free-tier tokens to free capacity?

maria: yes, applying rate limit rules now on edge. Should drop non-paid traffic by ~30%.

raj: drains complete for first 3 nodes, kube shows pods rescheduled. Two pods failed to start on remaining nodes due to OOM; captured logs:

```
E tensorflow: allocation failed: out of memory
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/serve.py", line 212, in <module>
    model.load()
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory
```

lee: note: pods failing -> increase retry limit? No, we should avoid thrashing. Keep backoff.

maria: spinning up low-priority cpu fallback for those jobs.

raj: cloud support pinged for quota bump. Also requested expedited review for 4 additional GPUs. ETA unknown but usually 30-90m.

incident-bot: summary so far: 1) Driver/kernel OOMs + Xid resets observed on multiple nodes -> effective GPU capacity reduced. 2) Autoscaler attempted nodes but hit cloud quota + rate-limits -> failed to recover. 3) Queue grew, causing higher latency and some 503s.

sasha: status check — what remains?

maria: fallback policies applied, batching reduced, rate limits for free-tier in place, drains in progress. Remaining risk: more nodes flapping if underlying hardware/driver issue persists. Need live metrics from telemetry to confirm stability.

lee: monitoring: set alert to watch (a) queue length, (b) Xid rate per node, (c) registered GPU capacity. Lower threshold for automatic rollback of autoscaler to prevent more API churn.

raj: note for postmortem: cloud quota exhaustion combined with driver instability -> two independent failures aligned. Recommend: pre-warm reserved capacity and a safety pool for autoscaler retries, plus better backoff on quota errors.

oliver: sending a short customer update now: "Mitigations applied: traffic throttling, fallback models, node isolation. We are monitoring; next update in 20 minutes."

incident-bot: oncall handoff scheduled in 40 minutes to lee -> next oncall: @maria.

maria: acknowledged, will be on for the handoff.

sasha: final note in-thread: log snapshots saved to /var/log/incidents/4448000000/gw-prod-high/ for post-incident review. Please avoid large downloads in the thread.

lee: good work. Keep updates brief; stick to timings. If we don't see queue back to normal in 30m escalate to exec communications.

oliver: customer impact update posted to status page (minor degrade). linking: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/4448000000

maria: queue trending down 22% in last 10m after throttles+fallback. Xid events still present but reduced frequency. Continuing to monitor.

raj: cloud support acknowledged quota request, investigating. They asked for exact request IDs for the failed creates; I posted those.

incident-bot: incident timeline saved. Closing note to follow postmortem once incident is resolved.

sasha: moving this to live incident channel for remaining coordination. Thanks all."
